title: Four places that organize the current oil brief
framing: These are sourced label anchors for guided reading, not boundaries, pipeline routes, shipping tracks or cargo locations.

stops.label: Strait of Hormuz
stops.why_it_matters: The brief's central disruption measure is the estimated change in oil flow through Hormuz.
stops.caveat: A strait is an area, not a point. This anchor must not be read as a route or vessel position.
stops.source_title: Wikidata Q79883 — coordinate location; EIA Figure 4 supplies geographic context

stops.label: Bab el-Mandeb
stops.why_it_matters: Its aggregate flow rose in the brief window, providing evidence of changed route use without proving one-for-one rerouting.
stops.caveat: A strait is an area, not a point. Aggregate movement cannot identify displaced Hormuz cargoes.
stops.source_title: Wikidata Q83318 — coordinate location; EIA Figure 6 supplies geographic context

stops.label: Strait of Malacca
stops.why_it_matters: It connects the global chokepoint view to East Asian import demand and the China evidence in this brief.
stops.caveat: A single label point cannot represent the roughly 930-kilometre strait or any individual voyage.
stops.source_title: Wikidata Q48359 — coordinate location; EIA Figure 2 supplies geographic context

stops.label: King Fahd Industrial Port, Yanbu
stops.why_it_matters: Yanbu is the export-side destination of Saudi Arabia's East-West crude pipeline in the current graph.
stops.caveat: The fixture's broader Yanbu terminal entity is anchored to the named industrial port; pipeline route geometry is still absent.
